page.mentor_intro: Modern asthma care favours inhaled corticosteroid-containing regimens, with as-needed ICS-formoterol or maintenance-and-reliever therapy rather than SABA alone. Severe asthma needs phenotyping and consideration of biologics, macrolides or triple inhaler therapy.

teaching_points.claim: The 2025 VA/DoD guideline strongly recommends inhaled corticosteroids and suggests ICS combined with a rapid-onset long-acting beta-agonist as both reliever and controller, with step-up by increasing ICS or adding a long-acting anticholinergic.

In poorly controlled asthma at GINA step 3 or 4, budesonide-formoterol maintenance and reliever therapy lengthened time to first severe exacerbation compared with stepping up or continuing maintenance ICS-LABA with SABA reliever.
Triple versus dual inhaler therapy in moderate to severe asthma was associated with fewer severe exacerbations and modest control gains, without differences in quality of life or mortality.
The ERS/ATS severe asthma guideline suggests a trial of chronic macrolide therapy for persistent symptoms at GINA step 5 and anti-IL-4/13 for severe eosinophilic or corticosteroid-dependent asthma.
Licensed asthma biologics reduce exacerbations and hospitalisations, improve lung function, control and quality of life, and limit systemic corticosteroid use, with greater effect in T2 inflammation.

The ACCP 2026 guideline gives seven recommendations on choosing a biologic, based on quality of life, lung function, exacerbation frequency, oral steroid use, endotype, biomarkers and comorbidities, while noting no comparative effectiveness trials.
Clinical remission is achievable for a minority on biologics, with lower rates in those with worse FEV1, longer disease, maintenance oral corticosteroids, depression or obesity.
A Spanish study found most guideline quality indicators of asthma care are not followed in practice.

uncertainties: Head-to-head comparative efficacy of biologics.

page.mentor_intro: Licensed asthma biologics reduce exacerbations and hospitalisations, improve lung function, control and quality of life, and spare oral steroids, especially in T2 inflammation. Choice rests on endotype, biomarkers and comorbidities because head-to-head trials are lacking; clinical remission is achievable for a minority.

teaching_points.claim: Licensed asthma biologics reduce exacerbations and hospitalisations, improve lung function, asthma control and quality of life, and limit systemic corticosteroid use, with greater effect in T2 inflammation.

The ACCP 2026 guideline gives seven recommendations on choosing a biologic based on quality of life, lung function, exacerbation frequency, oral steroid use, endotype, biomarkers and comorbidities, but no comparative effectiveness trials exist.

The EAACI systematic review found high certainty that benralizumab, dupilumab, mepolizumab and omalizumab reduce severe exacerbation rates, and benralizumab, dupilumab and mepolizumab reduce oral corticosteroid use.
The ERS/ATS guideline suggests anti-IL-4/13 for severe eosinophilic asthma and for corticosteroid-dependent asthma regardless of eosinophils.
Head-to-head comparisons show small effect size differences with wide confidence interval overlap, and direct pragmatic trials assessing remission are needed.
Clinical remission is achievable for a minority treated with biologics, with lower rates in worse FEV1, longer disease, maintenance oral steroids, depression and obesity.
Real-world anti-IL5 biologics improve outcomes with effect sizes similar to RCTs, though data are largely retrospective.

uncertainties: Comparative efficacy of biologics.

page.mentor_intro: Acute asthma care centres on bronchodilators and systemic corticosteroids; high-dose inhaled corticosteroids may add benefit, and IV magnesium helps children. Prevention depends on adherence, eosinophilic phenotype and inhaler technique.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis found moderate evidence that high-dose inhaled corticosteroids added to systemic corticosteroids reduce hospital admission (OR 0.73) in ED treatment of moderate-to-severe exacerbations.
In children, intravenous magnesium sulfate improved pulmonary function and reduced hospitalisation and further treatment, whereas nebulised magnesium had no significant effect.

The Italian paediatric acute-asthma guideline advises against epinephrine, allows IV magnesium sulfate in severe attacks or FEV1 below 60% unresponsive to inhaled therapy, allows heliox in life-threatening attacks, and does not recommend leukotriene receptor antagonists.
Adherence of 80% or more lowered the odds of severe exacerbation (OR 0.53), and discontinuing therapy raised it.
Blood eosinophils of 200 cells/microlitre or more are associated with exacerbation (a modifiable factor in asthma management).
Inhaler technique education reduced exacerbation rates in older adults with asthma or COPD (pooled risk ratio 0.71).
Oral timolol and infusion propranolol were associated with higher asthma attack risk and should be avoided in patients at risk of asthma.
GORD and asthma exacerbation are only weakly associated.

uncertainties: Optimal role of inhaled steroids in the emergency department.
case_hooks: Child with severe attack unresponsive to initial inhaled therapy.

Real-world JAK inhibitor outcomes match trials, and dupilumab should prompt reassessment when cutaneous lymphoma is suspected.

teaching_points.claim: The 2026 paediatric atopic dermatitis guideline conditionally recommends against topical antimicrobials and PUVA phototherapy and strongly recommends against systemic corticosteroids.
Real-world effectiveness and safety of JAK inhibitors in atopic dermatitis are comparable to clinical trials.
Dupilumab may unmask or exacerbate cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, particularly mycosis fungoides and Sezary syndrome, so consensus recommendations guide patient selection and reassessment.
The European living guideline update on atopic eczema includes JAK inhibitors (abrocitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib) and considerations for paediatric, pregnant and breastfeeding patients.
The ACG evidence-to-recommendation framework for mild and moderate atopic dermatitis weighs benefits, certainty, patient preferences and feasibility.
Increased pollutants and temperature extremes are associated with a higher population burden of atopic dermatitis.
Dupilumab in pregnancy showed no significant increase in miscarriage or congenital malformations, though evidence is limited.

uncertainties: Long-term safety of JAK inhibitors.

page.mentor_intro: Catheter ablation reduces mortality, stroke and heart failure hospitalisation compared with medical therapy in AF, including in AF with heart failure and in HFpEF. A 4-week blanking period may be optimal, and uninterrupted NOACs cut major bleeding periprocedurally.

teaching_points.claim: In AF with heart failure, catheter ablation reduces mortality and heart failure hospitalisation compared with medical therapy (RR 0.60 for hospitalisation).
Catheter ablation of AF significantly reduces death, stroke and hospitalisation compared with medical therapy alone.
In HFpEF with AF, catheter ablation showed cardiovascular morbidity and mortality benefits compared with standard medical therapy, and lower AF recurrence.
A 4-week blanking period may be the optimal cutoff after AF ablation, supporting revision of the current 3-month period.
Uninterrupted periprocedural NOACs are associated with low stroke or TIA and significantly less major bleeding than uninterrupted VKAs during AF ablation.
Most oesophageal injuries after AF ablation resolved conservatively, while a small percentage of type 2b lesions progressed to perforation or fistula.
A review compares guidelines and consensus documents on AF catheter ablation.

uncertainties: Early rhythm control beyond ablation is not in the retrieved excerpts.
mcq_angles: Ablation in AF with heart failure.
case_hooks: AF patient with HFrEF considering ablation versus drugs.

page.mentor_intro: DOACs are as effective as and often safer than warfarin in AF, including CKD (CrCl 15 and above); evidence is weaker in dialysis. DOACs should be standard in low-risk AF needing anticoagulation, with correct dosing, and device-detected AF also benefits modestly.

teaching_points.claim: DOACs may increase efficacy and improve safety versus VKAs in AF with CKD (CrCl 15-90), with at least similar results in kidney failure.
In stage 5 CKD, DOACs showed a significant reduction in stroke and a non-significant trend to less major bleeding than VKAs.
In haemodialysis patients with AF, DOACs versus warfarin comparisons need validation by further prospective studies given thrombotic and bleeding risks.
DOACs should be standard of care in low-risk AF patients needing anticoagulation, with dabigatran showing the best balance of stroke prevention and bleeding reduction in one analysis.
A network meta-analysis found no difference in major bleeding, thromboembolism or mortality between DOACs and VKAs, and no DOAC clearly more favourable than others.
Anticoagulation with edoxaban or apixaban reduces stroke in device-detected AF and increases major bleeding.
Off-label underdosed DOACs, particularly rivaroxaban, were associated with increased ischaemic stroke without reduced bleeding, so on-label dosing should be emphasised.
DOACs may be a feasible option in AF with cirrhosis, pending validation.

uncertainties: Best strategy in dialysis patients.
case_hooks: AF patient with CKD stage 4 on warfarin considering a DOAC.
page.gaps: CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED scoring, apixaban versus rivaroxaban head-to-head data and dose reduction criteria are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

A meta-analysis found gut microbiota dysbiosis in ankylosing spondylitis, suggesting a possible therapeutic target.

uncertainties: Optimal tapering strategy.
case_hooks: Young man with inflammatory back pain and sacroiliitis on MRI.

topic: Bacterial meningitis: empirical antibiotics, dexamethasone, LP contraindications, CSF interpretation

page.mentor_intro: Bacterial meningitis is time-critical: antibiotics later than two hours after presentation roughly double mortality. Case fatality has fallen over eighty years but remains high; molecular and host-marker tests may help when cultures are negative.

teaching_points.claim: In community-acquired bacterial meningitis, odds of mortality increase markedly when antibiotics are given later than two hours after presentation, and delay raised the odds of neurological impairment (aOR 1.79).
Case fatality of community-acquired bacterial meningitis has declined over the last century but a high burden remains.
Aetiology of bacterial meningitis differs by age group and region.
Metagenomic next-generation sequencing has moderate diagnostic accuracy for bacterial meningitis/encephalitis and may help when standard diagnosis fails.
16S/18S rRNA gene PCR with Sanger sequencing can diagnose non-growing pathogens and may change antibiotic treatment when cultures stay negative.
Heparin-binding protein has high diagnostic accuracy for bacterial infections including meningitis (sensitivity and specificity 87% at a cut-off of 32.868 ng/ml).
Febrile neonates have about twice the rate of bacteraemia and meningitis as febrile infants in the second month of life.

uncertainties: Role of adjunctive dexamethasone is not covered by the retrieved excerpts.

page.mentor_intro: Metabolic bariatric surgery is the benchmark for sustained weight and metabolic outcomes versus GLP-1 receptor agonists, which are useful adjuncts after surgery. Joint British guidance addresses diabetes around surgery, and regional blocks such as ESP reduce opioid use.

teaching_points.claim: Surgery is the most effective intervention for severe obesity and remains the benchmark for sustained metabolic and weight outcomes compared with GLP-1 receptor agonists, which are valuable non-invasive or adjunctive options.
GLP-1 receptor agonists after bariatric surgery give significant weight loss and cardiometabolic improvements versus placebo or lifestyle.
A Joint British guideline recommends specialist diabetes follow-up and inpatient diabetes care for people undergoing metabolic-bariatric surgery.
Ring augmentation in metabolic bariatric surgery is cautiously supported for selective use, particularly in Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, with low-quality evidence.
Erector spinae plane block reduces opioid consumption and middle and late postoperative pain after bariatric surgery compared with TAP block.
VA/DoD 2025 obesity guidance addresses GLP-1 agonists, endoscopic therapies and metabolic and bariatric surgery with stigma-informed, longitudinal care.
AI can enhance safety and efficiency in metabolic and bariatric surgery if clinician-led and rigorously validated.

uncertainties: Long-term evidence for ring augmentation.
case_hooks: Patient with BMI 42 and type 2 diabetes choosing between surgery and drugs.

topic: best initial test for suspected pulmonary embolism in a stable patient

page.mentor_intro: In a haemodynamically stable patient the first step is a pre-test probability assessment, then D-dimer in non-high probability, then imaging. Age-adjusted D-dimer and the YEARS algorithm reduce imaging while staying safe.

teaching_points.claim: Original and simplified Wells rules combined with age-adjusted D-dimer have similar performance for ruling out PE, and the simplified Wells rule is preferred for ease of use.
Age-adjusted D-dimer cutoffs combined with low clinical probability rule out PE with fewer false positives than conventional D-dimer, across 47,720 patients with non-high clinical probability.
The YEARS algorithm had pooled sensitivity of 96% and specificity of 50%, with a risk ratio of 0.78 for advanced imaging use, suggesting it is effective and safe.
D-dimer interpretation depends on assay performance characteristics, and international guidelines differ in how they allow age-adjusted and pretest-adjusted thresholds.
In pregnancy, introducing the pregnancy-adapted YEARS guideline increased investigation for PE, and over 5 years there were no known missed cases among women assessed with D-dimer alone.

In cancer patients, D-dimer with clinical decision rules had failure rates similar to standard imaging, with the highest yield (26%) from revised Geneva with age-adjusted D-dimer and the YEARS algorithm.
In COVID-19, D-dimer of at least 1000 micrograms/L may help select patients for CT pulmonary angiography.
Double low-dose CT pulmonary angiography is feasible, with reduced radiation and contrast dose without compromising diagnostic image quality.

page.mentor_intro: Licensed asthma biologics reduce exacerbations and hospitalisations, improve lung function, control and quality of life, and spare oral steroids, especially in T2 inflammation. Choice rests on endotype, biomarkers and comorbidities because head-to-head trials are lacking; clinical remission is achievable for a minority.

teaching_points.claim: Licensed asthma biologics reduce exacerbations and hospitalisations, improve lung function, asthma control and quality of life, and limit systemic corticosteroid use, with greater effect in T2 inflammation.

The ACCP 2026 guideline gives seven recommendations on choosing a biologic based on quality of life, lung function, exacerbation frequency, oral steroid use, endotype, biomarkers and comorbidities, but no comparative effectiveness trials exist.

The EAACI systematic review found high certainty that benralizumab, dupilumab, mepolizumab and omalizumab reduce severe exacerbation rates, and benralizumab, dupilumab and mepolizumab reduce oral corticosteroid use.
The ERS/ATS guideline suggests anti-IL-4/13 for severe eosinophilic asthma and for corticosteroid-dependent asthma regardless of eosinophils.
Head-to-head comparisons show small effect size differences with wide confidence interval overlap, and direct pragmatic trials assessing remission are needed.
Clinical remission is achievable for a minority treated with biologics, with lower rates in worse FEV1, longer disease, maintenance oral steroids, depression and obesity.
Real-world anti-IL5 biologics improve outcomes with effect sizes similar to RCTs, though data are largely retrospective.

uncertainties: Comparative efficacy of biologics.
case_hooks: Eosinophilic asthma with frequent exacerbations despite high-dose ICS-LABA.

page.mentor_intro: Borderline personality disorder carries high suicide risk, and dialectical behaviour therapy variants, including DBT-PTSD and DBT-PE, reduce PTSD and depressive symptoms. Digital interventions can help suicidal ideation and paranoia, and personality disorders relate to violence risk.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis reports prevalence of suicide ideation, attempt and suicide in borderline personality disorder, influenced by age and clinical setting, with the impact of comorbid depression unclear.
DBT variants (DBT-PTSD and DBT-PE) were effective in reducing PTSD symptom severity and comorbid depressive symptoms.
Digital interventions for BPD symptoms support transdiagnostic digital interventions for paranoia and suicidal ideation.
A consensus guideline lists recommended psychotherapies for adults with psychiatric disorders, summarising indications and therapeutic tasks.
Personality disorders are associated with violence and antisocial behaviour, so improving identification and treatment of comorbid substance misuse may reduce adverse outcomes.
SSRIs, psychotherapy and combinations were compared for non-suicidal self-injury, with depressive symptoms important to address in the first 3 months.
Guidelines for complex PTSD psychotherapies rate certainty of evidence as low.

teaching_points.claim: Early antitoxin administration reduces mortality in foodborne botulism, although some patients still develop respiratory failure, so prompt antitoxin and meticulous intensive care are essential.
CDC clinical guidelines recommend best practices for diagnosing, monitoring and treating foodborne, wound and inhalational botulism.
Human botulism immune globulin (BIG-IV) shortened hospital stay by about 6 weeks in infant botulism with no difference in adverse events or complications.
Anaphylactic reactions occur in 1-2% of botulinum antitoxin recipients and require epinephrine and antihistamine treatment.
In children, antitoxin recipients had better survival and serious adverse events were rare, and most deaths occurred early.
In pregnancy and postpartum, botulism needs a high level of suspicion, with preparation for possible intubation.
Heptavalent botulism antitoxin registry data specifically solicited bradycardia, hypersensitivity and serum sickness events.

A network meta-analysis found EBV and EBC effective but increasing pneumothorax, with EBV slightly increasing mortality and long-term survival data needed.
Lung volume reduction in severe emphysema on maximal medical treatment has clinically meaningful benefits to be weighed against adverse events.
A 2026 consensus statement gives practical guidance on patient selection and periprocedural management for valve therapy.
An expert statement updates prevention and management of pneumothorax associated with one-way valve therapy.
Coil treatment for severe emphysema improves exercise capacity, but the owner has stopped production.

uncertainties: Long-term survival data.

topic: CABG versus PCI multivessel coronary disease

page.mentor_intro: Meta-analyses suggest CABG gives sustained lower cumulative all-cause mortality than PCI in multivessel disease without left main involvement, particularly in diabetes and complex anatomy, with lower MI and repeat revascularisation but upfront stroke risk. Left main outcomes are comparable.

teaching_points.claim: An individual patient data meta-analysis showed sustained lower cumulative all-cause mortality with CABG than PCI for multivessel disease without left main involvement.
Mortality benefit of CABG over PCI was seen in diabetes and higher coronary complexity, with no benefit for CABG in left main disease.
CABG is associated with a significant benefit regarding future myocardial infarction versus PCI in multivessel or left main CAD.
In chronic total occlusion eligible for both strategies, CABG is associated with superior survival, fewer MI and fewer repeat revascularisations.
With left ventricular dysfunction, CABG has long-term benefits for mortality and revascularisation but higher upfront stroke rate.
In ACS with unprotected left main disease, CABG reduced repeat revascularisation with a trend to more stroke.
Alternative approaches to CABG such as hybrid revascularisation merit exploration for combined benefits.

uncertainties: Evidence on LV dysfunction is predominantly observational.

topic: CADASIL: genetic features, MRI findings, clinical course

page.mentor_intro: CADASIL is caused by NOTCH3 mutations (common arginine variants), with MRI changes and white matter alterations linked to cognition. In CADASIL migraine, beta-blockers may be relatively contraindicated, and cholinesterase inhibitors help vascular cognitive impairment generally.

teaching_points.claim: The most common NOTCH3 mutations causing CADASIL include p.R75P, p.R141C, p.R182C and p.R544C, with possible founder effects.
Cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 missense mutations can present with clinical CADASIL and typical MRI findings, with less anterior temporal lobe involvement.
In CADASIL migraine, antimigraine prophylaxis with beta-blockers may be contraindicated relative to other therapies, and controlled studies are needed.
White matter alterations relate to domain-specific cognitive impairment in cerebral small vessel disease.
The parahippocampal gyrus may be a reliably affected brain region in CADASIL.
Impaired neurovascular coupling is associated with cerebral small vessel disease including CAA and CADASIL.
Donepezil 5 mg improves cognition slightly in vascular cognitive impairment according to network meta-analysis.

page.mentor_intro: CPPD diagnosis uses conventional radiography and ultrasound as complementary tests, with international consensus definitions of imaging features and a G-CAN nomenclature clarifying chondrocalcinosis. Core outcome domains for chronic and recurrent CPPD have been agreed.

teaching_points.claim: Conventional radiography and ultrasonography showed great diagnostic accuracy for CPPD and should be regarded as complementary in the work-up.
An international group defined imaging features characteristic of CPPD on radiography, CT and dual-energy CT.
The 2026 G-CAN consensus resolves ambiguities, particularly about chondrocalcinosis, giving consistent research definitions.
A core domain set for chronic and recurrent CPPD supports joint pain, tenderness, swelling, acute CPP crystal arthritis flares, overall function and global disease activity as core domains.

teaching_points.claim: SGLT2 inhibitors improve kidney outcomes across the full spectrum of GFR and albuminuria, including stage 4 CKD or minimal albuminuria, among patients with type 2 diabetes, CKD or heart failure.
SGLT2 inhibitors significantly reduced the primary renal outcome in CKD patients, with differences by patient features and underlying disease.
SGLT2 inhibitors help delay progression of non-diabetic kidney disease.
Empagliflozin kidney benefits were evident regardless of diabetes status, heart failure status, cause of kidney disease or the size of the initial eGFR dip.
SGLT2 inhibitors in CKD reduce cardiovascular disease, heart-failure hospitalisation and all-cause death without increasing serious adverse events or UTIs but with more respiratory tract infections.
An MRA combined with an SGLT2 inhibitor gives greater reductions in albuminuria and blood pressure than an SGLT2 inhibitor alone, pending outcome trials.
The cardiovascular and kidney benefits of GLP-1 receptor agonists are consistent regardless of SGLT2 inhibitor use in type 2 diabetes.
Use of gliflozins in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes and CKD remains suboptimal compared with guidelines.

uncertainties: Benefit in kidney transplant recipients needs randomised trials.

Troponin is often elevated in ED patients with SVT but has low prognostic value for MACE.
A gap exists between guideline indications for wearable cardioverter-defibrillators and real-world prescribing.

page.mentor_intro: The 2026 HRS-led consensus statement covers cardiovascular implantable electronic device infection and lead management, and PET-CT is useful for diagnosing infection. Non-laser lead extraction is safer than laser, with timing of reimplantation affecting reinfection.

teaching_points.claim: The 2026 multisociety expert consensus statement update covers CIED lead management, tricuspid valve replacement considerations and standardised transvenous lead extraction approach and facilities.
18F-FDG PET-CT and leukocyte scintigraphy have high sensitivity and specificity for CIED infection, with PET-CT preferred when available.
Non-laser transvenous lead extraction has a better safety and efficacy profile than laser methods, with greater risk of SVC injury with laser sheaths.
Excimer laser sheath-assisted lead extraction has high success and low procedural mortality rates for leads needing advanced extraction.
Laser sheaths were associated with lower complete lead removal rate and a 9.3-fold higher risk of death compared with rotating sheaths in one meta-analysis.
Time to reimplantation may affect reinfection rates after CIED infection, though findings are exploratory.
European physicians show knowledge gaps and lack of confidence across stages of CIED care, requiring education and streamlined referral.

uncertainties: Optimal timing of reimplantation.
case_hooks: Pacemaker pocket infection with positive blood cultures.

topic: Cardiac myxoma: clinical features, embolism risk, surgical excision

page.mentor_intro: Cardiac myxoma has low surgical mortality (4.7 per 1000 person-years) and low recurrence, and timely excision is warranted. Embolism risk factors include an irregular tumour surface and narrow base, and cerebral aneurysm is a rare complication.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis of cardiac myxoma found late mortality of 4.7 per 1000 person-years and recurrence of 0.5 per 1000 person-years, with timely excision warranted once diagnosed.
Risk factors for embolism in cardiac myxoma include irregular tumour surface, atypical location, narrow base and raised fibrinogen, so early surgery may benefit such patients.
Cerebral aneurysms from atrial myxoma are rare but have serious long-term consequences, so patients should be monitored.
Acute arterial occlusion from tumour embolism is most likely lung cancer or atrial myxoma, and early revascularisation in selected cases can prevent severe complications.
Surgical approach choice depends on surgeon expertise, with routine postoperative echocardiography essential for residual or recurrent tumour.
Pulmonary valve myxoma needs early diagnosis and complete resection before heart failure symptoms.
Cardiac myxoma in Carney complex shows a role for key genes dysregulated in cardiac cells.

uncertainties: Long-term efficacy of minimally invasive and robotic approaches.
case_hooks: Young woman with a left atrial mass, syncope and embolic stroke.
page.gaps: Clinical triad (obstruction, embolism, constitutional symptoms), tumour plop and differential diagnosis are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

page.mentor_intro: Cardiac physiologic pacing and CRT are guided by the 2023 HRS/APHRS/LAHRS guideline. CRT enables guideline-directed therapy and reduces loop diuretic need in HFrEF, though CRT-D may not add benefit in non-ischaemic or older patients, and avoiding isolated trans-tricuspid RV leads limits valvular regurgitation.

teaching_points.claim: The 2023 HRS/APHRS/LAHRS guideline on cardiac physiologic pacing covers evaluation, implant, follow-up and optimisation of response, including paediatric use, and identifies knowledge gaps.
In HFrEF, CRT implantation was associated with enabled use and dose of heart failure therapy and decreased loop diuretic need.
The treatment effect of CRT-D on mortality improved from early to late studies, with CRT-D not superior in groups such as non-ischaemic and older patients.
Pacing strategies avoiding isolated trans-tricuspid RV leads may prevent incident or worsening valvular regurgitation and reduce mortality.
A systematic review of HFrEF guidelines found common comorbidities such as iron deficiency, AF, obesity, sleep-disordered breathing and frailty were addressed, and calls for harmonisation.
The Canadian CCS/CHRS guidelines support selection of patients for CIED implantation.

uncertainties: Selection of CRT-D versus CRT-P.
mcq_angles: QRS morphology and duration for CRT selection (not in excerpts).
case_hooks: HFrEF patient with LBBB and QRS 160 ms on optimal therapy.

topic: Cardiovascular outcomes in diabetes: SGLT2i and GLP-1 agonist trial evidence

page.mentor_intro: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce MACE and mortality in diabetes with peripheral artery disease without clear limb benefit, may lower the combined mortality-hospitalisation endpoint in HFpEF, and tirzepatide gives cardiovascular benefit comparable to GLP-1RAs. Early SGLT2 inhibitor use after MI reduces MACE, and combining the classes needs randomised trials.

teaching_points.claim: GLP-1 receptor agonists lower MACE and all-cause mortality in type 2 diabetes with peripheral artery disease but do not clearly benefit limb-specific outcomes.
GLP-1 receptor agonists may significantly lower the combined risk of mortality and hospitalisation in HFpEF, without a significant effect on all-cause mortality alone (HR 0.81).
Tirzepatide provides cardiovascular benefit at least comparable to established GLP-1RAs in type 2 diabetes.
Early initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors in acute MI significantly reduced MACE, with uncertainty on heart failure hospitalisation and no effect on all-cause mortality or non-fatal MI.
Combining SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists is supported by observational data, with randomised trials of combined versus monotherapy needed.
GLP-1 receptor agonists exert anti-inflammatory effects in type 2 diabetes.
GLP-1 receptor agonists are a potential option for obstructive sleep apnoea in obesity and type 2 diabetes if adverse events are tolerable.

uncertainties: Effect on muscle mass and functional skeletal muscle needs analysis.
case_hooks: Diabetic patient with prior MI choosing between SGLT2i and GLP-1RA.
page.gaps: Pivotal trial names (EMPA-REG, LEADER, SUSTAIN-6) and heart failure hospitalisation numbers are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

Interventions targeting both clinician support and patient access were most effective at improving medication prescription and lowering lipids in peripheral artery disease.
The International Lipid Expert Panel consensus gives lipid management guidance for primary and secondary stroke prevention.

Tenofovir alafenamide raises lipid levels in chronic hepatitis B, so lipid profiles should be monitored in high-risk patients.

topic: Carotid and vertebral artery dissection: antiplatelets vs anticoagulation paradigms

page.mentor_intro: Individual patient data meta-analysis found no significant difference between anticoagulants and antiplatelets in preventing early recurrent events after cervical artery dissection. Recurrence is low, thrombolysis should not be denied, and stenting is second-line.

teaching_points.claim: An IPD meta-analysis of two randomised trials found no significant difference between anticoagulants and antiplatelets in preventing early recurrent events in cervical artery dissection.
A systematic review calls for large randomised trials of anticoagulation versus antiplatelets in spontaneous cervical artery dissection, weighing stroke reduction and bleeding.
Recurrence of cervical artery dissection is low, and recurrence with ischaemia is even lower.
Patients with dissection-related ischaemic stroke should not be denied thrombolysis, pending large randomised studies.
A history of migraine is associated with an increased risk of cervical artery dissection.
Carotid stenting for cervical dissection has acceptable mortality and complication rates as a second-line treatment, with low-quality evidence.
Fibromuscular dysplasia has neurologic manifestations including dissection.

uncertainties: Optimal antithrombotic strategy.
case_hooks: Young adult with neck pain and Horner syndrome.
page.gaps: Imaging diagnosis, treatment duration and trauma versus spontaneous mechanisms are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

topic: Carpal tunnel syndrome: diagnosis and management

page.mentor_intro: AAOS/ASSH guidance covers carpal tunnel management, and D5W injection parallels corticosteroid injection with fewer adverse effects in mild-to-moderate disease. Neuromuscular ultrasound and electrodiagnostic studies are both used, with the choice shared with patients.

teaching_points.claim: The AAOS/ASSH guideline summary gives practical recommendations for carpal tunnel syndrome management and highlights gaps in the literature.

D5W injection parallels corticosteroids in pain, symptom severity, electrodiagnostic measures and nerve area, with lower adverse effects, recommended as a preferred option for mild to moderate carpal tunnel syndrome.
Choice between neuromuscular ultrasound and electrodiagnostic studies should involve shared decision-making weighing accuracy, availability, cost and tolerability.
An expert consensus gives the role of neuromuscular ultrasound alongside electrodiagnostic tests in polyneuropathies and carpal tunnel, with future work to define when ultrasound can stand alone.
The global prevalence of carpal tunnel syndrome is high, highlighting the need for effective management strategies.

A guideline addresses anti-infective vaccination strategies in patients with haematological malignancies, including those on CAR T cells.

topic: Central Nervous System Vasculitis (PACNS): digital subtraction angiography, cyclophosphamide regimens

page.mentor_intro: The 2023 ESO guideline is the first comprehensive European GRADE guideline on PACNS. Angiography and biopsy-defined disease differ, diagnostic tests often disagree, and adult PACNS has frequent relapses and high mortality.

teaching_points.claim: The ESO guideline is the first comprehensive European guideline on primary angiitis of the CNS using GRADE methodology, to assist clinicians in choosing management strategies.
Where both biopsy and angiography were performed in primary CNS vasculitis, disagreement between them was more than five times more likely than agreement, so diagnostic criteria may need revision.
There are distinct clinical features between biopsy-defined and angiography-defined primary CNS vasculitis, which may aid selection of invasive tests.
Adult PACNS is associated with frequent relapses and high mortality, with symptomatic epilepsy, prolonged biopsy time window and CD20 expression linked to recurrence.
A systematic review of childhood PACNS recommends induction including trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and maintenance with mycophenolate, though no grade-A evidence exists.
Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related CNS vasculitis is rare and needs early immunosuppression.
Tumefactive PACNS can mimic glioblastoma.

uncertainties: Revision of diagnostic criteria.
case_hooks: Young adult with headaches, multifocal strokes and lymphocytic CSF.

Sleep-related breathing disorders are common in dementia, particularly Alzheimer's and Parkinson's dementia.

topic: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA): microbleeds, lobar haemorrhages, diagnostic criteria

page.mentor_intro: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy is found in a substantial share of lobar intracerebral haemorrhage. Microbleed burden and distribution, and disseminated cortical superficial siderosis, identify survivors at higher risk of recurrent haemorrhage, and microbleeds raise haemorrhage risk after thrombolysis.

teaching_points.claim: CAA prevalence is 50-57% in patients with lobar intracerebral haemorrhage, with large heterogeneity across neuropathology and MRI protocols.
Microbleed burden and distribution on MRI identify ICH survivors with higher recurrence risk.
Disseminated cortical superficial siderosis (more than 3 sulci) increases future ICH risk in symptomatic CAA survivors (Class III evidence).
Increasing microbleed burden is associated with higher risk of ICH and poor 3-6 month functional outcome after intravenous thrombolysis.
CSF patterns of Aβ42, Aβ40, tau and p-tau differ in CAA versus Alzheimer's disease and may serve as biomarkers.
In CAA-related inflammation, MRI findings are most prevalent and about 34% carry homozygous ApoE ε4/ε4.

uncertainties: Biomarker validation in larger cohorts.
case_hooks: Elderly patient with lobar haemorrhage and multiple cortical microbleeds.
page.gaps: Boston criteria, antithrombotic decisions and management of CAA-related inflammation are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

topic: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST): risk factors, anticoagulation choices

page.mentor_intro: Cerebral venous thrombosis is managed per the 2024 Canadian Stroke Best Practice module and Chinese Stroke Association guideline. Meta-analyses suggest DOACs have similar efficacy and safety to vitamin K antagonists, with caution pending randomised confirmation.

teaching_points.claim: The Canadian Stroke Best Practice Recommendations 7th edition include a cerebral venous thrombosis module with implementation resources and performance measures.
The Chinese Stroke Association guideline summarises evidence for CVST diagnosis, treatment and secondary prevention.
A meta-analysis found DOACs in CVT have similar efficacy and safety to VKAs with better recanalisation rate.
Another meta-analysis of DOACs versus VKAs in CVT urges caution because of limited randomised data, small sample and rare events.
COVID-19-associated CVT is a diagnostic challenge needing high suspicion; evidence on pathophysiology and prevention is scarce.
Population-based CVT incidence is heterogeneous across studies, with Canadian incidence lower than elsewhere.
The ACR Appropriateness Criteria address imaging in stroke and related conditions.

uncertainties: DOAC versus VKA awaiting more randomised data.
case_hooks: Young woman on oral contraception with headache and venous infarct.
page.gaps: Heparin in acute phase, treatment duration, MR venography and risk-factor workup are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

The French radiation oncology society recommends indications and techniques for external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy in cervical cancer.
Self-collected vaginal specimens for HPV testing expand screening options and access for under-screened people, requiring laboratory and clinical workflow changes.
When self-collected vaginal specimens are used for HPV testing, a 3-year interval should be followed, with screening-exit stipulations for higher-risk women.
The WHO guideline supports screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions as part of the global strategy to eliminate cervical cancer.

topic: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy: clinical signs, surgical decompression indications

page.mentor_intro: The 2025 AO Spine guideline states surgery is valid for mild degenerative cervical myelopathy and anterior or posterior approaches give similar clinical benefit with different complication profiles. Clinical signs should prompt imaging, and laminoplasty versus fusion trade lordosis preservation against complications.

teaching_points.claim: The AO Spine guideline notes surgical treatment is effective and a valid option for mild DCM, with anterior and posterior approaches giving similar benefit but different complications.
Clinical signs suggesting cord compression should prompt neuroimaging to confirm or refute DCM.
Anterior decompression with fusion preserved cervical lordosis better than laminoplasty, with more surgical complications, and similar neurological recovery.
Laminoplasty versus laminectomy shows better C5 radiculopathy and superficial infection results with laminoplasty.
Predictors of kyphotic deformity after laminoplasty are reviewed, with a preoperative risk score proposed as future work.
Gait speed is the only spatio-temporal parameter that improved significantly after decompression in DCM.
WFNS and Italian guidance lists contemporary recommendations for cervical spondylotic myelopathy.
Understanding the natural history of DCM is a research priority, with MRI-related pathologies common in healthy people.

uncertainties: Natural history of asymptomatic cord compression.
case_hooks: Older patient with clumsy hands, gait disturbance and hyperreflexia.
page.gaps: Hoffmann sign, mJOA severity grading and indications for conservative care are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

topic: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease: CMT1A duplication, nerve conduction patterns

page.mentor_intro: The 2025 clinical practice guidelines for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease cover diagnosis and management, with exercise, orthotic adaptation and tendon transfer, and state follow-up is clinical without routine ancillary testing. Paediatric guidance and a French gene-list consensus support multidisciplinary care and molecular diagnosis.

teaching_points.claim: CMT guidelines address exercise, orthotic adaptation and conservative surgeries such as tendon transfer, with clinical-only follow-up and no routine ancillary testing.
A paediatric CMT guideline advocates improved access to multidisciplinary care.
A consensus statement on CMT surgery gives an approach to cavovarus deformity at Level V evidence.
A French consensus gene list for inherited neuropathies has 93 definitive and 34 limited genes.
Neurofilament light chain is a blood-based marker of neuronal injury in peripheral neuropathies.
CMT prevalence studies are heterogeneous, with higher rates in males and Northern Europe, and need clearer diagnostic criteria.

uncertainties: Epidemiology varies by method and country.

page.mentor_intro: ICI cardiotoxicity has high mortality, and early recognition, ICI cessation and prompt corticosteroids are recommended though randomised evidence is absent. Systematic reviews report systematic cardiology screening before treatment and feasible re-challenge after recovery.

teaching_points.claim: A meta-analysis found cardiovascular adverse event mortality with ICIs remains high, with early recognition, ICI cessation and prompt corticosteroids advised in absence of randomised evidence.
Systematic cardiological screening is advocated before PD-1, PD-L1 and CTLA-4 inhibitor therapy.
Analysis of case reports suggests glucocorticoids can be reduced or stopped after recovery and ICI re-challenge may be feasible after resolution.
A review compared high-dose with low-dose steroids for ICI-associated myocarditis, suggesting therapy duration be tailored and combination therapy considered in steroid resistance.
Thymic alterations are associated with incidence and seriousness of ICI myotoxicities.
TripleM syndrome (myocarditis, myositis, myasthenia) management has limited evidence and needs consensus definitions.
In lung cancer, ICI plus chemotherapy raised cardiotoxicity risk versus single ICI, while dual immunotherapy did not.

uncertainties: Optimal steroid dose and second-line agents.
case_hooks: Melanoma patient on nivolumab with troponin rise and conduction block.
page.gaps: Diagnostic criteria (biopsy, cardiac MRI), troponin surveillance and abatacept or other second-line therapy are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

page.mentor_intro: A 2024 multidisciplinary Japanese guideline updates prevention and treatment of cancer-drug extravasation, classifying drugs by tissue injury. Neonatal and contrast extravasation guidance emphasises clinical diagnosis, and surgical referral by clinical severity rather than extravasated volume.

teaching_points.claim: A multidisciplinary guideline from the Japanese Society of Clinical Oncology updates prevention and treatment of extravasation of cancer drug therapy and classifies drugs by tissue injury.
A neonatal extravasation guideline with an educational programme was tested in a before-and-after study, and needs periodic education incorporated into nurse induction.
For contrast medium extravasation, diagnosis is mostly clinical, outcomes mostly favourable, and surgical referral should rest on clinical severity not volume.
Peripheral IV catheter non-infectious complications, including infiltration, are a common cause of catheter failure in adults and children.

uncertainties: Evidence for antidotes is not covered by the retrieved excerpts.

page.mentor_intro: CINV prevention is guided by SEOM guidance covering multiday regimens, oral treatments and radiation-induced emesis. Adding olanzapine to a triplet regimen helps in highly emetogenic chemotherapy, and paediatric guidelines address breakthrough and anticipatory CINV.

teaching_points.claim: Adding olanzapine to 5-HT3 antagonist, NK1 antagonist and dexamethasone triplet therapy is useful in preventing nausea and vomiting from highly emetogenic chemotherapy with minimal adverse effects.
The SEOM emesis guideline covers antiemetic prophylaxis options including oral treatments, multiday regimens and radiation-induced emesis.
The ASCO cannabis guideline notes uncertainty about whether cannabinoids improve supportive care outcomes in adults with cancer.
A paediatric guideline recommends options for acute and delayed CINV, including patients unable to receive dexamethasone or an NK1 antagonist, and identifies evidence gaps.
Paediatric breakthrough CINV guidance recommends using antiemetics that controlled breakthrough to prevent refractory CINV.
Hypnosis, systematic desensitisation, relaxation and lorazepam are conditionally recommended for secondary prevention of anticipatory CINV in children.
Systematic desensitisation may reduce anticipatory CINV in adults, pending further research.
Acupuncture may improve acute and delayed vomiting control but certainty of evidence is very low.

uncertainties: Non-drug measures have very low certainty.
case_hooks: Patient on cisplatin with delayed nausea despite ondansetron.
page.gaps: Emetogenic risk classification, specific NK1 antagonist doses and the MASCC/ASCO regimen by risk level are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

teaching_points.claim: Rhinovirus-induced bronchiolitis was more strongly associated than RSV bronchiolitis with recurrent wheeze and childhood asthma.
Childhood asthma prevalence is highest in Oceania and lower in Eurasia, with modifiable risk factors identified.
Exposure to particulate matter is associated with developing asthma and wheeze in children, supporting measures to reduce particle pollution.
Black and organic carbon and ammonium in PM2.5 mainly contributed to increased childhood asthma risk.
Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection is positively associated with childhood asthma, though causal mechanisms are unclear.
Mediterranean diet adherence shows a trend to inverse association with childhood asthma with low certainty.

uncertainties: Causality of infection and diet associations.

topic: Cholera and Vibrio infections: oral rehydration, doxycycline, epidemic control, vaccination

page.mentor_intro: Oral killed cholera vaccines give high-certainty protection with about 40% vaccine efficacy at two years. Paediatric diarrhoea guidance restricts antibiotics to dysentery-like symptoms, suspected cholera with severe dehydration or comorbidities, and antimicrobial resistance, including tetracycline, is rising in V. cholerae.

teaching_points.claim: Oral killed cholera vaccines reduce cholera, with overall vaccine efficacy about 40% at both one- and two-year follow-up in a trial of 204,700 participants (high-certainty evidence).

A Chinese paediatric diarrhoea guideline recommends zinc for children over 6 months in deficient regions and restricts antibiotics to dysenteric symptoms, suspected cholera with severe dehydration, or comorbidities.
Antimicrobial resistance is rising in V. cholerae, especially in low-income and endemic areas, so surveillance and appropriate susceptibility testing are crucial.
Tetracycline resistance among clinical V. cholerae isolates requires monitoring when choosing treatment.
Ciprofloxacin, azithromycin and other agents showed the best effectiveness against V. cholerae isolates in a resistance meta-analysis.
Non-cholera Vibrio infections carry a high burden in South Asia, with antibiotic-resistant and ESBL strains reported.

uncertainties: Emerging resistance patterns.
case_hooks: Patient with profuse watery stool in an outbreak area.
page.gaps: Oral rehydration and intravenous fluid regimens (the core of therapy) are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

CBT and hypnotherapy may be considered for childhood functional abdominal pain disorders.
ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN guidelines for IBS and functional abdominal pain identified major evidence gaps and incentivise large paediatric trials.
A multidisciplinary expert consensus guides primary care providers in diagnosing and managing paediatric functional abdominal pain disorders.
A probiotics meta-analysis in children with functional abdominal pain disorders found similar adverse event withdrawals between probiotic and placebo.
Vitamin D supplementation may help IBS with potential efficacy and good safety, pending further trials.
Medical cannabis recommendations place it as third- or fourth-line therapy in chronic noncancer pain after detailed discussion of benefits and harms.
Video capsule endoscopy is a complementary test for GI bleeding, Crohn's or coeliac disease with negative or inconclusive prior studies.

Antibody-mediated rejection is a critical unmet treatment need across heart and lung allografts.

teaching_points.claim: Plasma donor-derived cell-free DNA accuracy for acute rejection in kidney allografts is limited by heterogeneity, but it is a valuable biomarker for antibody-mediated rejection.
A risk-adapted approach to HLA delisting and imlifidase-enabled deceased-donor kidney transplantation addresses highly sensitised patients after kidney-preserving pathways are exhausted.
A JACC position statement highlights contemporary diagnosis and therapy of antibody-mediated rejection after heart transplantation, including complement-mediated injury and cytokine pathways.
The ISHLT scientific statement on pulmonary antibody-mediated rejection stresses better treatments as a critical unmet need and proposes a more precise definition.
An ISHLT consensus conference prepared a platform for further studies of antibodies and AMR in transplant patients.
A clinical consensus statement on heart transplantation covers cardiac allograft vasculopathy, infections and malignancies.
AASLD/AST guidance on liver transplant graft-related complications highlights the need to optimise management including recurrence prevention of alcohol-associated and metabolic liver disease.

uncertainties: Treatment of antibody-mediated rejection.
case_hooks: Kidney transplant recipient with rising creatinine and donor-specific antibodies.
page.gaps: Kidney-specific chronic allograft nephropathy, interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity and Banff classification are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

topic: Chronic aortic regurgitation: surveillance intervals and surgical timing

page.mentor_intro: In chronic aortic regurgitation, vena contracta width and LV volumes reliably identify significant disease, while CMR and global longitudinal strain add prognostic information in asymptomatic patients. Reviews suggest surgery timed earlier than current guidelines may give survival benefit, but randomised trials are lacking.

teaching_points.claim: A simplified echo approach using vena contracta width and LV volumes can reliably identify significant AR when compared with CMR.
Global longitudinal strain is a prognostic biomarker in asymptomatic moderate-to-severe AR with preserved LVEF and may help timing of surgery, though thresholds need validation.
Multi-parameter CMR predicts aortic valve surgery as an endpoint in chronic AR.
Myocardial remodelling assessment beyond volumes and function may identify irreversible myocardial injury earlier.
Studies of AR, AS and mixed disease found long-term survival benefit from surgery earlier than current guideline timing, but RCTs are required.

uncertainties: Optimal timing of surgery in asymptomatic patients.
case_hooks: Asymptomatic young adult with severe AR and LVEF 55%.

A systematic review of CCS clinical practice guidelines calls for stronger multidisciplinary efforts toward higher-quality evidence-based guidelines.

Atherogenic index of plasma is linked to CAD risk, severity and prognosis, with optimal cut-offs unclear.
Triglyceride-glucose index is associated with in-stent restenosis after PCI.

teaching_points.claim: AGA best practice advice says symptom improvement on PPI in extraesophageal reflux may arise from non-acid mechanisms and does not confirm GERD.
In children with chronic cough, GERD treatment should not be used without clinical features of GERD, and paediatric GERD guidelines should guide investigation.
The CHEST paediatric chronic cough guideline now has high-quality evidence for some management aspects, with further primary care studies needed.
Aetiologies of chronic cough in children differ from adults and depend on age and setting.
The CHEST guideline on cough due to asthma and non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis addresses non-invasive airway inflammation measurement and treatment.
Evidence for managing chronic cough in interstitial lung disease is limited.
The Chinese national cough guideline covers evaluation, diagnosis, and empirical and symptomatic treatment of chronic cough.

uncertainties: Evidence for ILD cough therapy is limited.
case_hooks: Non-smoker with chronic dry cough and normal chest radiograph.

In children, acute-onset CIDP is suspected when Guillain-Barré syndrome follows a prolonged course.

uncertainties: Long-term immunotherapy needs after remission.

teaching_points.claim: The 2026 AHA/ACC/ADA/ASN guideline addresses prevention, detection, evaluation and management of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome for cardiologists, endocrinologists, nephrologists and primary care.
A living guideline on type 2 diabetes therapeutics covers cardiovascular, kidney-related and weight loss effects, and notes cost and availability limit implementation.
The KDIGO 2026 guideline gives recommendations for management of anaemia in chronic kidney disease.
A consensus report on frailty in CKD links serial frailty measurement to decisions on assisted home dialysis and transplant eligibility.
Renal dose adjustment guideline adherence is inconsistent, and non-adherence to dosing recommendations was associated with adverse consequences and higher healthcare use.
An Indian consensus aims to standardise online haemodiafiltration practice in kidney replacement therapy.

uncertainties: Strategies to improve prescribing safety.
case_hooks: Patient with diabetes, CKD stage 3 and rising cardiovascular risk.

page.mentor_intro: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce kidney outcomes across the range of GFR and albuminuria, including stage 4 CKD and in non-diabetic CKD, and reduce cardiovascular events and mortality. Adding an MRA lowers albuminuria and blood pressure further, and GLP-1 agonist benefits are independent of SGLT2 inhibitor use.

teaching_points.claim: SGLT2 inhibitors improve kidney outcomes across the full spectrum of GFR and albuminuria, including stage 4 CKD or minimal albuminuria, among patients with type 2 diabetes, CKD or heart failure.
SGLT2 inhibitors significantly reduced the primary renal outcome in CKD patients, with differences by patient features and underlying disease.
SGLT2 inhibitors help delay progression of non-diabetic kidney disease.
Empagliflozin kidney benefits were evident regardless of diabetes status, heart failure status, cause of kidney disease or the size of the initial eGFR dip.
SGLT2 inhibitors in CKD reduce cardiovascular disease, heart-failure hospitalisation and all-cause death without increasing serious adverse events or UTIs but with more respiratory tract infections.
An MRA combined with an SGLT2 inhibitor gives greater reductions in albuminuria and blood pressure than an SGLT2 inhibitor alone, pending outcome trials.
The cardiovascular and kidney benefits of GLP-1 receptor agonists are consistent regardless of SGLT2 inhibitor use in type 2 diabetes.
Use of gliflozins in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes and CKD remains suboptimal compared with guidelines.

uncertainties: Benefit in kidney transplant recipients needs randomised trials.
mcq_angles: eGFR dip does not predict loss of benefit.
case_hooks: Patient with diabetes and eGFR 28 with albuminuria considering SGLT2 inhibitor.

BTK inhibitors need baseline and 3-monthly ECG and blood pressure monitoring for AF and hypertension, and pneumococcal vaccination is recommended in haematological malignancy.

teaching_points.claim: The Canadian evidence-based guideline gives consensus recommendations on first-line CLL treatment.
A 2024 workshop consensus complements existing guidelines with US real-world expert approaches to CLL/SLL treatment selection.
For BTK inhibitor cardiovascular adverse events, blood pressure monitoring and ECG at baseline and every 3 months are recommended, with close haematologist-cardiologist collaboration.
In a meta-analysis of newer BTK inhibitors, zanubrutinib may be preferred over acalabrutinib monotherapy, but randomised trials are needed.
A venetoclax meta-analysis found no specific infection that would benefit from routine antimicrobial prophylaxis or pre-emptive testing, with higher neutropenia risk in AML.
Pneumococcal vaccination is recommended for all patients with lymphoma, AML and adults with ALL.
An international consensus addresses diagnosis, evaluation and research for Richter transformation.
Saudi guidelines cover CLL diagnosis, staging and first-line and relapsed/refractory management.

uncertainties: Direct randomised comparison of BTK inhibitors.

page.mentor_intro: The 2025 Chinese CML guideline favours treatment minimising toxicity while ensuring efficacy, with allogeneic transplant for multidrug TKI resistance or intolerance and advanced phases. An expert consensus defines TKI intolerance in chronic phase, TKI haematological adverse event rates differ by drug, and ponatinib needs cardiovascular risk management.

teaching_points.claim: The Chinese CML guideline emphasises minimising toxicity and improving quality of life while ensuring efficacy, with allogeneic transplant valuable for multidrug TKI resistance or intolerance and advanced phases.
An expert consensus defines treatment intolerance of TKIs in chronic-phase CML to standardise care and shared decision-making.
Haematological adverse event prevalence differs between TKIs, in an order of ponatinib above bosutinib, imatinib and nilotinib in pooled analysis.
French recommendations propose practical measures to minimise cardiovascular events in ponatinib-treated patients.
Imatinib is associated with reduced height growth in paediatric CML, independent of pubertal status.
ABCG2 c.421C>A is associated with imatinib trough plasma levels in GIST and CML.

uncertainties: Optimal TKI choice given toxicity profiles.
mcq_angles: Growth effect of imatinib in children.
case_hooks: Chronic-phase CML patient intolerant of imatinib.
page.gaps: Response milestones, BCR::ABL1 monitoring, treatment-free remission and blast crisis management are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

page.mentor_intro: European recommendations standardise CMML diagnosis, prognostication and treatment. For transplant candidates, EBMT advises upfront transplantation without prior disease-modifying therapy where possible, and hypomethylating agents decitabine and azacitidine appear comparably effective. ASXL1 mutation predicts poorer prognosis.

teaching_points.claim: International expert guidelines set standardised diagnostic and prognostic procedures and therapeutic choices for adult CMML.
EBMT recommends upfront transplantation without prior disease-modifying treatment, whenever possible, in CMML transplant candidates regardless of blast count.
Decitabine and azacitidine appear comparably effective and safe in CMML, but direct comparison needs a randomised trial.
In CMML, TET2 mutated with ASXL1 wild-type genotype was most favourable for survival; ASXL1 mutation raised hazard.
ASXL1 mutations are associated with poor prognosis in MDS and aid risk stratification.
SETBP1 mutation predicts poor prognosis in MDS and CMML but not CNL.
SRSF2 mutation predicted shorter survival in MDS but showed no prognostic effect in CMML.

uncertainties: Hypomethylating agent comparative efficacy.
case_hooks: Older patient with persistent monocytosis and cytopenias.
page.gaps: Diagnostic criteria (monocyte count thresholds), CPSS-Mol scoring and ruxolitinib or other therapies are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

page.mentor_intro: The 2025 European guideline covers diagnosis and treatment of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, and ASGE suggests endoscopic therapy over surgery for specified chronic pancreatitis complications. ESPEN advises screening and supplementing at-risk patients for nutrient deficiencies and acknowledging osteoporosis, and an international consensus standardises pain assessment.

teaching_points.claim: European guidelines summarise prevalence, clinical impact and diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for pancreatic exocrine insufficiency across clinical conditions.

ESPEN advises patients with chronic pancreatitis be considered at risk, screened and supplemented for deficiencies, with osteoporosis and fracture risk acknowledged and preventive measures considered.
ASGE suggests endoscopic therapy over surgery for the chronic pancreatitis indications addressed in its guideline.
An international consensus recommends standardised pain assessment in chronic pancreatitis together with quality of life and psychiatric comorbidities.
A clinical practice guideline covers acute and chronic pancreatitis, with uncomplicated long-term care by primary care and gastroenterology.
Gut microbiota in chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer show fewer beneficial and more pathogenic species, with therapeutic implications unproven.
A consensus report defines fibrosis-related conditions in the pancreas, aiming to close knowledge gaps.

uncertainties: Optimal pain management strategies.
case_hooks: Patient with chronic pain, steatorrhoea and pancreatic calcification.
page.gaps: Pancreatic enzyme dosing, diabetes management and ductal stone therapy details are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

page.mentor_intro: The international EAACI/GA2LEN/EDF/WAO guideline (2018, updated 2022 and 2026) defines, classifies and manages urticaria. Higher pretreatment total IgE is associated with better omalizumab response, WAO defines CSU clinical remission as at least 6 months symptom-free without drugs, and head-to-head trials of H1-refractory therapies are lacking.

teaching_points.claim: The international urticaria guideline defines, classifies and sets evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for urticaria subtypes, and has been updated in 2022 and 2026.
Pretreatment total serum IgE in CSU is associated with clinical response to omalizumab.
World Allergy Organization defines clinical remission of CSU as total resolution of signs and symptoms without pharmacotherapy for at least 6 months, a definition needing validation.
For H1 antihistamine-refractory CSU, high-quality head-to-head trials with harmonised outcomes are needed to inform guidelines.
Dupilumab has reports of effectiveness in several inflammatory skin diseases including chronic spontaneous urticaria.
A critical appraisal of urticaria guidelines found quality gains from rigorous GRADE rating, methodologist involvement and external review.

uncertainties: Comparative efficacy of refractory CSU therapies.
case_hooks: Patient with daily wheals for 8 weeks despite standard antihistamine.
page.gaps: Antihistamine up-dosing, ciclosporin and weaning schedule are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

page.mentor_intro: CTEPH should be managed in an experienced multidisciplinary centre combining pulmonary endarterectomy, balloon pulmonary angioplasty and drugs. BPA is safe and effective in selected patients, with mostly mild complications, and appears to improve exercise capacity earlier than PEA while PEA may achieve better haemodynamics at 12 months.

teaching_points.claim: CTEPH patients should be treated in a multidisciplinary centre experienced in pulmonary endarterectomy, balloon pulmonary angioplasty and pharmacological therapy.
Meta-analysis shows BPA is a safe and effective option in select CTEPH patients with improved haemodynamics and exercise tolerance and low major complication rates.
BPA complications occurred in 14% of procedures and were mostly mild, with more thoracic complications when mean PAP exceeded 45 mmHg.
In comparison, BPA may give greater early exercise capacity improvement than PEA, while PEA may be superior for haemodynamics at 12 months.
A clinical consensus statement on BPA companions the ESC/ERS guidelines and standardises complication definitions.
Cologne consensus update reserves PEA and BPA for specialised centres, with inoperable patients candidates for targeted drug therapy and BPA.
After venous thromboembolism therapy, patients should be reassessed for symptoms of post-thrombotic syndrome or CTEPH.
A CTEPH consensus statement is a literature review with expert opinion because comparative trials are limited.

uncertainties: Head-to-head BPA versus PEA trials are limited.
case_hooks: Persistent dyspnoea six months after pulmonary embolism.
page.gaps: V/Q scanning for diagnosis, riociguat and anticoagulation duration are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

page.mentor_intro: The 2020 ACR guideline uses GRADE and patient preferences, and ACP and EULAR recommend discussing urate-lowering therapy with a predefined urate target in recurrent gout. Guideline inconsistencies exist across guidelines, and gout in CKD has important knowledge gaps.

teaching_points.claim: The 2020 ACR gout guideline uses GRADE methodology and patient preferences to direct clinicians on gout management.
ACP strongly recommends discussing benefits, harms, costs and preferences before starting urate-lowering therapy with concomitant prophylaxis in recurrent attacks (moderate-quality evidence).
EULAR recommendations aim to reach a predefined urate target using non-pharmacological and pharmacological treatment.

page.mentor_intro: Clinical findings for compartment syndrome have limited and heterogeneous accuracy, and regional analgesia after lower leg trauma has a guideline from European anaesthesia and trauma societies. For rhabdomyolysis, EAST conditionally recommends aggressive fluid resuscitation and against bicarbonate or mannitol, and gluteal compartment syndrome in neurologically intact patients may be observed.

teaching_points.claim: A diagnostic meta-analysis of compartment syndrome finds clinical findings need revisiting with new prospective studies to characterise statistical value (Level III).
A guideline on regional analgesia for lower leg trauma addresses risk of acute compartment syndrome, noting patients' right to refuse treatment and neither surgeon nor anaesthetist having veto.

EAST conditionally recommends aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation in rhabdomyolysis to improve acute renal failure outcomes and lessen dialysis, and conditionally recommends against bicarbonate or mannitol.
In gluteal compartment syndrome, neurologically intact patients may be managed medically with neurological surveillance, and fasciotomy does not affect mortality.
Prehospital tourniquet use for civilian extremity vascular trauma decreased mortality without significantly increasing amputation or compartment syndrome.
Consensus recommendations aim to shorten recognition-to-action time in acute distal limb ischaemia after large-bore arterial access.

uncertainties: Diagnostic accuracy of individual clinical signs.

page.mentor_intro: The Endocrine Society guideline covers 21-hydroxylase deficiency management. teaching_points.claim: The Endocrine Society guideline gives best-practice recommendations for 21-hydroxylase deficiency CAH, considering patient safety, quality of life, cost and utilisation.
Non-classic CAH may need different therapeutic strategies at different follow-up stages, and genetic counselling can prevent CAH in offspring.
Individuals with CAH have a high prevalence of cardiovascular and metabolic risk factors, with evidence based on surrogate outcomes.
Adrenal tumours, particularly myelolipomas, are prevalent in CAH, associated with late diagnosis or poor control, so imaging may be considered especially with abdominal pain.
After genital reconstructive surgery in females with CAH, most were sexually active and satisfied but some reported impaired sexual experience; evidence certainty is very low.
Differences of sex development warrant multidisciplinary care and long-term psychosexual support, with variable gender identity outcomes.
French consensus on adrenal insufficiency notes DHEA androgen replacement may be offered and monitoring relies on signs of under- and over-dosage.

uncertainties: Long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

FVC is the preferred lung physiology measure for trials, DLCO did not meet OMERACT criteria, though DLCO and TLC should not yet be discounted. CT honeycombing predicts respiratory mortality, and the role of biopsy and lavage is uncertain.

teaching_points.claim: FVC is recommended as the lung physiology instrument for SSc-ILD trials, while DLCO did not meet OMERACT criteria.
Evidence suggests DLCO and TLC should not yet be discounted as surrogate markers of SSc-ILD progression despite FVC preference.
CT honeycombing extent predicts respiratory mortality in SSc-ILD, and CT predictors of progression need further study.
Lung biopsy for SSc-ILD is poorly studied, and its value for refining prognosis and therapy is unknown.
Bronchoalveolar lavage findings relate to severe pulmonary disease and worse prognosis in SSc, though added value over non-invasive tests is unknown.
Global SSc epidemiology shows ILD in 35-55% and pulmonary arterial hypertension in 6-12%, with need for early detection in expert centres.
MUC5B rs35705950 predicts susceptibility to idiopathic interstitial pneumonia and familial IIP but showed no significant relation with SSc-ILD.

uncertainties: Use of DLCO as outcome.
case_hooks: Patient with diffuse systemic sclerosis and falling FVC.
page.gaps: Other CTD-ILD (rheumatoid arthritis, myositis), treatments (mycophenolate, nintedanib, tocilizumab) are not covered by the retrieved excerpts.

topic: Conservative oxygen therapy in mechanically ventilated patients

page.mentor_intro: Pooled analyses find conservative oxygen therapy does not consistently reduce mortality in ICU, ventilated, acute medical or post-cardiac-arrest patients. An earlier IOTA meta-analysis found liberal oxygen increases mortality, and benefit may be limited to fewer ventilator-free days or organ failure; targets above SpO2 94-96% may be unfavourable.

teaching_points.claim: The IOTA meta-analysis of acutely ill adults found liberal oxygen increases mortality, with supplemental oxygen possibly unfavourable above SpO2 94-96%.
Conservative oxygen therapy did not reduce all-cause mortality in ICU patients, affecting only mechanical-ventilation-free days.
A meta-analysis found conservative oxygen did not reduce mortality but decreased ventilation time, new organ failure and renal replacement therapy risk in critical care.
For ventilated ICU patients, conservative oxygen was not significantly superior to liberal oxygen on clinical outcomes.
In acutely ill medical patients, conservative oxygen therapy was not associated with decreased mortality.
After cardiac arrest, conservative oxygen did not decrease mortality, improve neurologic recovery or shorten ICU stay in a meta-analysis of RCTs.
An individual-level analysis after cardiac arrest found lower mortality with conservative oxygen with low to very low certainty.
Implementing a conservative oxygenation guideline changed attitudes and practice and improved adherence to targets.

uncertainties: Effect in specific populations.
case_hooks: Ventilated ICU patient with SpO2 100%.
page.gaps: Exact target ranges used in trials (e.g. PaO2 or SpO2 thresholds) are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

topic: Constrictive pericarditis: haemodynamic features, pericardiectomy indications

page.mentor_intro: BNP and NT-proBNP are lower in constrictive pericarditis than restrictive cardiomyopathy, and Mayo Clinic echocardiographic criteria have good accuracy for differentiating them. Tuberculosis is an important cause, especially with HIV in Africa, and pericardiectomy outcomes are worse in non-idiopathic aetiologies.

teaching_points.claim: BNP and NT-proBNP were significantly lower in constrictive pericarditis than restrictive cardiomyopathy, with BNP showing good pooled diagnostic accuracy.
All echocardiographic parameters from the Mayo Clinic criteria have good diagnostic accuracy for differentiating constrictive pericarditis from restrictive cardiomyopathy.
HIV infection complicates a significant portion of constrictive pericarditis in Africa, and early mortality has improved globally but remains high.

In pericardiectomy for constrictive pericarditis, post-radiation and other non-idiopathic aetiologies carry higher mortality than idiopathic, with heterogeneity and a possible need for randomised trials.
Pericardiectomy for constrictive tuberculous pericarditis has operative mortality with significant heterogeneity and methodological concerns.
Tuberculous cardiac involvement is frequent and can lead to heart failure, constrictive pericarditis or death, so early detection of complications is key.
Cochrane evidence on tuberculous pericarditis interventions shows low-certainty findings, with colchicine and steroid effects uncertain.
Intrapericardial fibrinolysis to prevent complications of effusion has very low certainty of efficacy and safety.

uncertainties: Steroid benefit in TB pericarditis.
case_hooks: Patient with HIV, ascites, raised JVP and pericardial calcification.
page.gaps: Respirophasic septal shift, Kussmaul sign, CT or MRI findings and timing of pericardiectomy are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

topic: Continuous EEG monitoring in the ICU: non-convulsive status epilepticus

page.mentor_intro: Continuous EEG is advised for patients with altered mental status after convulsive status epilepticus, while diagnostic criteria for nonconvulsive status epilepticus in comatose patients remain unsettled. cEEG also aids neonatal seizure assessment, and neurophysiology contributes to prognostication after hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy.

teaching_points.claim: Guidelines and consensus statements recommend continuous EEG monitoring for patients with altered mental status after convulsive status epilepticus.
The modified Salzburg and updated ACNS criteria for nonconvulsive status epilepticus in comatose patients have unresolved diagnostic accuracy.
Continuous EEG should be used to diagnose neonatal seizures and assess severity, remission and drug efficacy.
Very low cortical SSEP amplitudes (approximately 0.5 µV or less) strongly predict poor outcome after hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy, though not yet in guidelines.
Diagnosis and management of adult status epilepticus in resource-limited settings is non-uniform, highlighting the need for appropriate guidelines.
In COVID-19, EEG commonly shows encephalopathy correlating with severity, with frontal findings proposed as a biomarker.
A practical approach to ICU encephalopathy notes dexmedetomidine is effective for delirium in ventilated patients, while haloperidol has minimal effect.

uncertainties: NCSE criteria in coma.
case_hooks: Patient not waking after convulsive seizure ended.
page.gaps: Recommended duration of monitoring, quantitative EEG and subclinical seizure treatment thresholds are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.

topic: Continuous glucose monitoring CGM: time-in-range targets, hybrid closed loop

page.mentor_intro: CGM adds benefit across settings: in hospitalised non-critically ill adults it improves control and reduces hypoglycaemia over point-of-care testing, in pregnancy it lowers HbA1c and possibly large-for-gestational-age risk, and in non-insulin-treated type 2 diabetes it supports lifestyle change. An Italian guideline supports wider T2D use.

teaching_points.claim: In non-critically ill hospitalised adults with diabetes, adding CGM to point-of-care testing for insulin dosing gave superior glycaemic control and less hypoglycaemia.
CGM in pregnancy reduces HbA1c and possibly large-for-gestational-age risk, with greatest benefit in type 1 diabetes, then gestational diabetes.
CGM in non-insulin-treated type 2 diabetes improves outcomes and patient experience, reduces resource use, and has acceptable cost-effectiveness.
CGM guides lifestyle choices and nutrition in type 2 diabetes with benefits for glycaemia and body weight.
An Italian guideline supports a shift to wider use of CGM in type 2 diabetes, with CGM becoming mandatory for people on insulin therapy and reimbursement needing adaptation.
Real-world evidence shows commercially available automated insulin delivery systems differ in glycaemic outcomes including time in range, with age influencing outcomes.
An international guideline defines study design, comparator measurements and minimum accuracy requirements for CGM system assessment.

uncertainties: Real-world evidence biases for AID systems.
case_hooks: Pregnant woman with type 1 diabetes and variable glucose.
page.gaps: Time-in-range targets, AGP metrics and indications by diabetes type are not stated in the retrieved abstract excerpts.
